newsitem.title: CHINA: China wins contract to develop Sudan oil field.
newsitem.headline: China wins contract to develop Sudan oil field.

text.p: The China National Petroleum Corp (Sinopec) has won a contract to develop a Sudan oilfield that will eventually pump out 15 million tonnes of oil a year, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The project, to be launched in March, would develop an oilfield with an area of 50,000 square km (19,300 sq miles) and proven reserves of 220 million tonnes, Xinhua quoted Zeng Xingqiu, deputy-director of Sinopec's international cooperation bureau, as saying.
"It will be the largest oil field construction project China has ever undertaken overseas, as well as one of the largest oil field cooperation projects in the world," Zeng said.
China would launch 18 large petroleum and petrochemical projects in other countries with a total contracted investment of $750 million this year, Zeng said.
The projects included an oil refinery in Malaysia, oil and gas pipelines in Turkmenistan, a gas pipeline in Thailand and oil and gas wells in Mongolia and Bangladesh, he said.
China would also be involved in an oil storage facility and restoring an oil refinery in Kuwait, and would carry out oil prospecting in Canada, Peru and Venezuela, he said.

"In Kuwait alone, China has passed preliminary qualification examination for undertaking another five petroleum and petrochemical projects this year, with total investment topping $3.0 billion," he said.

China would try to ease its domestic oil and gas shortages by exploiting overseas markets and importing limited amounts of oil and gas, Xinhua quoted Qin Anmin, president of the China Petroleum Engineering Construction Corp, as saying.
